# AFP Psykiatrisk Klinik 2 - AUH

AFP Psykiatrisk Klinik 2 - AUH is a clinical unit reporting into the Danish ADHD-databasen (ADHD database), the national clinical quality database that tracks treatment courses for patients with ADHD, including — starting in 2024 — adult patients. The unit's name situates it within the psychiatric services connected to Aarhus Universitetshospital (AUH), and its results are cited as part of the database's rollout of two new quality indicators covering adult ADHD treatment courses.

The clinic's most significant recorded result concerns Indikator 10, a newly introduced measure of whether a patient's social support needs were assessed no later than 120 days after the start of treatment. AFP Psykiatrisk Klinik 2 - AUH achieved a 45 percent fulfilment rate on this indicator (108 out of 238 treatment courses, with a confidence interval of 39–52 percent) [^src1]. This falls well short of the national quality target of 90 percent, and it also sits below the broader national average of 37 percent reported at the same time, though regional results nationally ranged widely from 14 to 52 percent [^src1]. Because this was the first time Indikator 10 had been reported, the steering group overseeing the database discussed possible causes for the shortfall, including registration practices and data quality issues originating in child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals, and resolved to work on improving registration practice going forward [^src1].

The clinic also appears in the database's reporting on Indikator 11, which measures the share of adult treatment courses in which the patient was receiving ADHD medication within 120 days of starting a structured treatment package ("pakkeforløb") — another measure introduced for the first time in 2024 following the database's expansion to include adult patients [^src2]. On this indicator, AFP Psykiatrisk Klinik 2 - AUH recorded a substantially higher fulfilment rate of 78 percent (185 out of 238 treatment courses, confidence interval 72–83 percent) [^src2]. Regional results for this indicator varied considerably across Denmark, from 85 percent in Region Nordjylland down to 37 percent in Region Hovedstaden, a spread the source material attributes primarily to differences in registration practice rather than genuine clinical variation [^src2].

Together, these two data points show a clinic performing far below the national development target on the newly measured social-support-assessment indicator, while performing comparatively well — though still below is not indicated for Indicator 11 — on the medication-timeliness indicator. No further relationships, claims, or timeline events for this entity are documented in the corpus beyond these two indicator results.
